solution:
[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key writes the third term as \(\frac{11}{4}(x+3)\) with the \(\log\) dropped; it should be \(\frac{11}{4}\log|x+3|\). The answer below is correct.]

Let \(\frac{x^2+2}{(x-1)(x+2)(x+3)}=\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{B}{x+2}+\frac{C}{x+3}\).
Then \(x^2+2=A(x+2)(x+3)+B(x-1)(x+3)+C(x-1)(x+2)\).
Put \(x=1:\ 3=A(3)(4)\Rightarrow A=\frac{1}{4}\).
Put \(x=-2:\ 6=B(-3)(1)\Rightarrow B=-2\).
Put \(x=-3:\ 11=C(-4)(-1)\Rightarrow C=\frac{11}{4}\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{4}\int\frac{dx}{x-1}-2\int\frac{dx}{x+2}+\frac{11}{4}\int\frac{dx}{x+3}\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{4}\log|x-1|-2\log|x+2|+\frac{11}{4}\log|x+3|+c\).

Put \(t=x^2\). Then \(\frac{x^2}{(x^2+1)(x^2-2)(x^2+3)}=\frac{t}{(t+1)(t-2)(t+3)}=\frac{A}{t+1}+\frac{B}{t-2}+\frac{C}{t+3}\).
So \(t=A(t-2)(t+3)+B(t+1)(t+3)+C(t+1)(t-2)\).
Put \(t=-1:\ -1=A(-3)(2)\Rightarrow A=\frac{1}{6}\).
Put \(t=2:\ 2=B(3)(5)\Rightarrow B=\frac{2}{15}\).
Put \(t=-3:\ -3=C(-2)(-5)\Rightarrow C=-\frac{3}{10}\).
Restoring \(t=x^2\):
\(I=\frac{1}{6}\int\frac{dx}{x^2+1}+\frac{2}{15}\int\frac{dx}{x^2-2}-\frac{3}{10}\int\frac{dx}{x^2+3}\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{6}\tan^{-1}x+\frac{2}{15}\cdot\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}\log\left|\frac{x-\sqrt2}{x+\sqrt2}\right|-\frac{3}{10}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{\sqrt3}\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{6}\tan^{-1}x+\frac{1}{15\sqrt2}\log\left|\frac{x-\sqrt2}{x+\sqrt2}\right|-\frac{\sqrt3}{10}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{\sqrt3}+c\).

Factorise the denominator: \(6x^2+13x-63=(3x-7)(2x+9)\).
Let \(\frac{12x+3}{(3x-7)(2x+9)}=\frac{A}{3x-7}+\frac{B}{2x+9}\Rightarrow 12x+3=A(2x+9)+B(3x-7)\).
Put \(x=\frac{7}{3}:\ 31=A\left(\frac{41}{3}\right)\Rightarrow A=\frac{93}{41}\).
Put \(x=-\frac{9}{2}:\ -51=B\left(-\frac{41}{2}\right)\Rightarrow B=\frac{102}{41}\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{93}{41}\int\frac{dx}{3x-7}+\frac{102}{41}\int\frac{dx}{2x+9}\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{31}{41}\log|3x-7|+\frac{51}{41}\log|2x+9|+c\).

Factorise: \(4-3x-x^2=-(x^2+3x-4)=-(x+4)(x-1)\).
\(\therefore \frac{2x}{4-3x-x^2}=\frac{-2x}{(x+4)(x-1)}=\frac{A}{x+4}+\frac{B}{x-1}\), so \(-2x=A(x-1)+B(x+4)\).
Put \(x=-4:\ 8=A(-5)\Rightarrow A=-\frac{8}{5}\).
Put \(x=1:\ -2=B(5)\Rightarrow B=-\frac{2}{5}\).
\(\therefore I=-\frac{8}{5}\int\frac{dx}{x+4}-\frac{2}{5}\int\frac{dx}{x-1}\).
\(\therefore I=-\frac{8}{5}\log|x+4|-\frac{2}{5}\log|x-1|+c\).

The integrand is improper (numerator degree = denominator degree), so divide first:
\(\frac{x^2+x-1}{x^2+x-6}=1+\frac{5}{x^2+x-6}=1+\frac{5}{(x+3)(x-2)}\).
Let \(\frac{5}{(x+3)(x-2)}=\frac{A}{x+3}+\frac{B}{x-2}\Rightarrow 5=A(x-2)+B(x+3)\).
Put \(x=-3:\ 5=A(-5)\Rightarrow A=-1\); put \(x=2:\ 5=B(5)\Rightarrow B=1\).
\(\therefore I=\int 1\,dx-\int\frac{dx}{x+3}+\int\frac{dx}{x-2}\).
\(\therefore I=x-\log|x+3|+\log|x-2|+c=x+\log\left|\frac{x-2}{x+3}\right|+c\).

Numerator degree > denominator degree, so divide first:
\(\frac{6x^3+5x^2-7}{3x^2-2x-1}=(2x+3)+\frac{8x-4}{3x^2-2x-1}\).
Factorise \(3x^2-2x-1=(3x+1)(x-1)\) and split \(\frac{8x-4}{(3x+1)(x-1)}=\frac{A}{3x+1}+\frac{B}{x-1}\), so \(8x-4=A(x-1)+B(3x+1)\).
Put \(x=1:\ 4=B(4)\Rightarrow B=1\); put \(x=-\frac{1}{3}:\ -\frac{20}{3}=A\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right)\Rightarrow A=5\).
\(\therefore I=\int(2x+3)\,dx+5\int\frac{dx}{3x+1}+\int\frac{dx}{x-1}\).
\(\therefore I=x^2+3x+\frac{5}{3}\log|3x+1|+\log|x-1|+c\).

Factorise \(4x^2-1=(2x-1)(2x+1)\), so the integrand is \(\frac{12x^2-2x-9}{(2x-1)(2x+1)(x+3)}=\frac{A}{2x-1}+\frac{B}{2x+1}+\frac{C}{x+3}\).
Then \(12x^2-2x-9=A(2x+1)(x+3)+B(2x-1)(x+3)+C(2x-1)(2x+1)\).
Put \(x=\frac{1}{2}:\ -7=A(2)\left(\frac{7}{2}\right)=7A\Rightarrow A=-1\).
Put \(x=-\frac{1}{2}:\ -5=B(-2)\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)=-5B\Rightarrow B=1\).
Put \(x=-3:\ 105=C(-7)(-5)=35C\Rightarrow C=3\).
\(\therefore I=-\int\frac{dx}{2x-1}+\int\frac{dx}{2x+1}+3\int\frac{dx}{x+3}\).
\(\therefore I=-\frac{1}{2}\log|2x-1|+\frac{1}{2}\log|2x+1|+3\log|x+3|+c\).

Multiply numerator and denominator by \(x^4\): \(\frac{1}{x(x^5+1)}=\frac{x^4}{x^5(x^5+1)}\).
Put \(t=x^5\), so \(dt=5x^4\,dx\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{5}\int\frac{dt}{t(t+1)}=\frac{1}{5}\int\left(\frac{1}{t}-\frac{1}{t+1}\right)dt=\frac{1}{5}\left(\log|t|-\log|t+1|\right)\).
Restoring \(t=x^5\):
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{5}\log\left|\frac{x^5}{x^5+1}\right|+c\).

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives the first term as \(\frac{11}{\sqrt{5}}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{2}\); since it comes from \(\frac{11}{x^2+5}\), the argument must be \(\frac{x}{\sqrt{5}}\), not \(\frac{x}{2}\). The answer below is correct.]

Factorise: \(x^4+9x^2+20=(x^2+4)(x^2+5)\). Put \(t=x^2\) to split:
\(\frac{2x^2-1}{(x^2+4)(x^2+5)}=\frac{2t-1}{(t+4)(t+5)}=\frac{A}{t+4}+\frac{B}{t+5}\Rightarrow 2t-1=A(t+5)+B(t+4)\).
Put \(t=-4:\ -9=A(1)\Rightarrow A=-9\); put \(t=-5:\ -11=B(-1)\Rightarrow B=11\).
Restoring \(t=x^2\):
\(I=-9\int\frac{dx}{x^2+4}+11\int\frac{dx}{x^2+5}\).
\(\therefore I=-9\cdot\frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{2}+11\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt5}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{\sqrt5}=-\frac{9}{2}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{2}+\frac{11}{\sqrt5}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{\sqrt5}+c\).

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key's second log is \(\frac{5}{2\sqrt{2}}\log\left|\frac{x+\sqrt{2}}{x-\sqrt{2}}\right|\); the standard form \(\int\frac{dx}{x^2-2}\) gives the reciprocal ratio \(\frac{x-\sqrt{2}}{x+\sqrt{2}}\), so the book's term has the wrong sign. The answer below is correct.]

Put \(t=x^2\): \(\frac{x^2+3}{(x^2-1)(x^2-2)}=\frac{t+3}{(t-1)(t-2)}=\frac{A}{t-1}+\frac{B}{t-2}\Rightarrow t+3=A(t-2)+B(t-1)\).
Put \(t=1:\ 4=A(-1)\Rightarrow A=-4\); put \(t=2:\ 5=B(1)\Rightarrow B=5\).
Restoring \(t=x^2\): \(\frac{x^2+3}{(x^2-1)(x^2-2)}=\frac{-4}{x^2-1}+\frac{5}{x^2-2}\), and \(\frac{-4}{x^2-1}=\frac{2}{x+1}-\frac{2}{x-1}\).
\(\therefore I=2\int\frac{dx}{x+1}-2\int\frac{dx}{x-1}+5\int\frac{dx}{x^2-2}\).
\(\therefore I=2\log|x+1|-2\log|x-1|+\frac{5}{2\sqrt2}\log\left|\frac{x-\sqrt2}{x+\sqrt2}\right|+c\).

Put \(t=x^2\), so \(dt=2x\,dx\). The numerator gives \(2x\,dx=dt\):
\(\therefore I=\int\frac{dt}{(2+t)(3+t)}=\int\left(\frac{1}{2+t}-\frac{1}{3+t}\right)dt=\log|2+t|-\log|3+t|\).
Restoring \(t=x^2\):
\(\therefore I=\log\left|\frac{x^2+2}{x^2+3}\right|+c\).

Note \(4^x=(2^x)^2\). Put \(t=2^x\), so \(dt=2^x\log 2\,dx\), i.e. \(2^x\,dx=\frac{dt}{\log 2}\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{\log 2}\int\frac{dt}{t^2-3t-4}=\frac{1}{\log 2}\int\frac{dt}{(t-4)(t+1)}\).
Now \(\frac{1}{(t-4)(t+1)}=\frac{1}{5}\left(\frac{1}{t-4}-\frac{1}{t+1}\right)\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{5\log 2}\left(\log|t-4|-\log|t+1|\right)\).
Restoring \(t=2^x\):
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{5\log 2}\log\left|\frac{2^x-4}{2^x+1}\right|+c\).

Let \(\frac{3x-2}{(x+1)^2(x+3)}=\frac{A}{x+1}+\frac{B}{(x+1)^2}+\frac{C}{x+3}\).
Then \(3x-2=A(x+1)(x+3)+B(x+3)+C(x+1)^2\).
Put \(x=-1:\ -5=B(2)\Rightarrow B=-\frac{5}{2}\).
Put \(x=-3:\ -11=C(4)\Rightarrow C=-\frac{11}{4}\).
Compare coefficients of \(x^2:\ 0=A+C\Rightarrow A=\frac{11}{4}\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{11}{4}\int\frac{dx}{x+1}-\frac{5}{2}\int\frac{dx}{(x+1)^2}-\frac{11}{4}\int\frac{dx}{x+3}\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{11}{4}\log|x+1|+\frac{5}{2(x+1)}-\frac{11}{4}\log|x+3|+c\).

Factorise \(x^3+2x^2+x=x(x+1)^2\).
Let \(\frac{5x^2+20x+6}{x(x+1)^2}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{x+1}+\frac{C}{(x+1)^2}\).
Then \(5x^2+20x+6=A(x+1)^2+Bx(x+1)+Cx\).
Put \(x=0:\ 6=A\Rightarrow A=6\).
Put \(x=-1:\ -9=C(-1)\Rightarrow C=9\).
Compare coefficients of \(x^2:\ 5=A+B\Rightarrow B=-1\).
\(\therefore I=6\int\frac{dx}{x}-\int\frac{dx}{x+1}+9\int\frac{dx}{(x+1)^2}\).
\(\therefore I=6\log|x|-\log|x+1|-\frac{9}{x+1}+c\).

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives \(\frac{1}{8}\log\left|\frac{x^6(x^3+3)}{(3x^3+1)^3}\right|\); the coefficient should be \(\frac{1}{6}\) and the numerator factor should be \((x^3+1)\) (from the factorisation \((x^3+1)(3x^3+1)\)), not \((x^3+3)\). The answer below is correct.]

Factorise \(1+4x^3+3x^6=(1+x^3)(1+3x^3)\), and multiply numerator and denominator by \(x^2\):
\(\frac{1}{x(1+4x^3+3x^6)}=\frac{x^2}{x^3(1+x^3)(1+3x^3)}\).
Put \(t=x^3\), so \(dt=3x^2\,dx\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{3}\int\frac{dt}{t(1+t)(1+3t)}\).
Split \(\frac{1}{t(1+t)(1+3t)}=\frac{1}{t}+\frac{B}{1+t}+\frac{C}{1+3t}\); putting \(t=0,-1,-\frac{1}{3}\) gives \(B=\frac{1}{2},\ C=-\frac{9}{2}\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{3}\left[\log|t|+\frac{1}{2}\log|1+t|-\frac{3}{2}\log|1+3t|\right]\).
Restoring \(t=x^3\):
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{3}\log|x^3|+\frac{1}{6}\log|1+x^3|-\frac{1}{2}\log|1+3x^3|+c\).

Factorise \(x^3-1=(x-1)(x^2+x+1)\).
Let \(\frac{1}{(x-1)(x^2+x+1)}=\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{Bx+C}{x^2+x+1}\Rightarrow 1=A(x^2+x+1)+(Bx+C)(x-1)\).
Put \(x=1:\ 1=3A\Rightarrow A=\frac{1}{3}\).
Compare \(x^2:\ 0=A+B\Rightarrow B=-\frac{1}{3}\); constant: \(1=A-C\Rightarrow C=-\frac{2}{3}\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{3}\int\frac{dx}{x-1}-\frac{1}{3}\int\frac{x+2}{x^2+x+1}\,dx\).
For the second, \(x+2=\frac{1}{2}(2x+1)+\frac{3}{2}\) and \(x^2+x+1=\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2\), so
\(\int\frac{x+2}{x^2+x+1}\,dx=\frac{1}{2}\log(x^2+x+1)+\frac{3}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\tan^{-1}\frac{2x+1}{\sqrt3}=\frac{1}{2}\log(x^2+x+1)+\sqrt3\,\tan^{-1}\frac{2x+1}{\sqrt3}\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{3}\log|x-1|-\frac{1}{6}\log(x^2+x+1)-\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\tan^{-1}\frac{2x+1}{\sqrt3}+c\).

Put \(t=\sin x\), so \(dt=\cos x\,dx\), and \(\cos^2 x=1-\sin^2 x=1-t^2\).
Denominator: \(5-4\sin x-\cos^2 x=5-4t-(1-t^2)=t^2-4t+4=(t-2)^2\).
\(\therefore I=\int\frac{3t-2}{(t-2)^2}\,dt\).
Put \(u=t-2\Rightarrow 3t-2=3u+4\):
\(I=\int\frac{3u+4}{u^2}\,du=\int\left(\frac{3}{u}+\frac{4}{u^2}\right)du=3\log|u|-\frac{4}{u}\).
Restoring \(u=t-2=\sin x-2\):
\(\therefore I=3\log|\sin x-2|-\frac{4}{\sin x-2}+c\).

\(\sin x+\sin 2x=\sin x+2\sin x\cos x=\sin x(1+2\cos x)\).
Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sin x\):
\(\frac{1}{\sin x(1+2\cos x)}=\frac{\sin x}{\sin^2 x(1+2\cos x)}=\frac{\sin x}{(1-\cos^2 x)(1+2\cos x)}\).
Put \(t=\cos x\), so \(dt=-\sin x\,dx\):
\(I=-\int\frac{dt}{(1-t)(1+t)(1+2t)}\).
Split \(\frac{1}{(1-t)(1+t)(1+2t)}=\frac{1}{6(1-t)}-\frac{1}{2(1+t)}+\frac{4}{3(1+2t)}\).
Integrating this and then applying the outer minus sign:
\(I=\frac{1}{6}\log|1-t|+\frac{1}{2}\log|1+t|-\frac{2}{3}\log|1+2t|\).
Restoring \(t=\cos x\):
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{6}\log|1-\cos x|+\frac{1}{2}\log|1+\cos x|-\frac{2}{3}\log|1+2\cos x|+c\).

\(2\sin x+\sin 2x=2\sin x+2\sin x\cos x=2\sin x(1+\cos x)\).
Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sin x\):
\(\frac{1}{2\sin x(1+\cos x)}=\frac{\sin x}{2\sin^2 x(1+\cos x)}=\frac{\sin x}{2(1-\cos x)(1+\cos x)^2}\).
Put \(t=\cos x\), so \(dt=-\sin x\,dx\):
\(I=-\frac{1}{2}\int\frac{dt}{(1-t)(1+t)^2}\).
Split \(\frac{1}{(1-t)(1+t)^2}=\frac{1}{4(1-t)}+\frac{1}{4(1+t)}+\frac{1}{2(1+t)^2}\), so
\(\int\frac{dt}{(1-t)(1+t)^2}=-\frac{1}{4}\log|1-t|+\frac{1}{4}\log|1+t|-\frac{1}{2(1+t)}\).
\(\therefore I=-\frac{1}{2}\left[-\frac{1}{4}\log|1-t|+\frac{1}{4}\log|1+t|-\frac{1}{2(1+t)}\right]\).
Restoring \(t=\cos x\):
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{8}\log|1-\cos x|-\frac{1}{8}\log|1+\cos x|+\frac{1}{4(1+\cos x)}+c\).

\(\sin 2x+\cos x=2\sin x\cos x+\cos x=\cos x(2\sin x+1)\).
Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\cos x\):
\(\frac{1}{\cos x(2\sin x+1)}=\frac{\cos x}{\cos^2 x(2\sin x+1)}=\frac{\cos x}{(1-\sin^2 x)(2\sin x+1)}\).
Put \(t=\sin x\), so \(dt=\cos x\,dx\):
\(I=\int\frac{dt}{(1-t)(1+t)(1+2t)}\).
Split \(\frac{1}{(1-t)(1+t)(1+2t)}=\frac{1}{6(1-t)}-\frac{1}{2(1+t)}+\frac{4}{3(1+2t)}\).
\(\therefore I=-\frac{1}{6}\log|1-t|-\frac{1}{2}\log|1+t|+\frac{2}{3}\log|1+2t|\).
Restoring \(t=\sin x\):
\(\therefore I=-\frac{1}{6}\log|1-\sin x|-\frac{1}{2}\log|1+\sin x|+\frac{2}{3}\log|1+2\sin x|+c\).

Multiply numerator and denominator by \(\sin x\):
\(\frac{1}{\sin x(3+2\cos x)}=\frac{\sin x}{\sin^2 x(3+2\cos x)}=\frac{\sin x}{(1-\cos^2 x)(3+2\cos x)}\).
Put \(t=\cos x\), so \(dt=-\sin x\,dx\):
\(I=-\int\frac{dt}{(1-t)(1+t)(3+2t)}\).
Split \(\frac{1}{(1-t)(1+t)(3+2t)}=\frac{1}{10(1-t)}+\frac{1}{2(1+t)}-\frac{4}{5(3+2t)}\).
Integrating this and then applying the outer minus sign:
\(I=\frac{1}{10}\log|1-t|-\frac{1}{2}\log|1+t|+\frac{2}{5}\log|3+2t|\).
Restoring \(t=\cos x\):
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{10}\log|1-\cos x|-\frac{1}{2}\log|1+\cos x|+\frac{2}{5}\log|3+2\cos x|+c\).

Put \(t=e^x\), so \(dt=e^x\,dx\), and \(e^{2x}=t^2\).
\(\therefore I=\int\frac{5\,dt}{(t+1)(t^2+9)}\).
Let \(\frac{5}{(t+1)(t^2+9)}=\frac{A}{t+1}+\frac{Bt+C}{t^2+9}\Rightarrow 5=A(t^2+9)+(Bt+C)(t+1)\).
Put \(t=-1:\ 5=10A\Rightarrow A=\frac{1}{2}\).
Compare \(t^2:\ 0=A+B\Rightarrow B=-\frac{1}{2}\); constant: \(5=9A+C\Rightarrow C=\frac{1}{2}\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{2}\int\frac{dt}{t+1}-\frac{1}{2}\int\frac{t-1}{t^2+9}\,dt\).
Now \(\int\frac{t-1}{t^2+9}\,dt=\frac{1}{2}\log(t^2+9)-\frac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}\frac{t}{3}\), so
\(I=\frac{1}{2}\log|t+1|-\frac{1}{4}\log(t^2+9)+\frac{1}{6}\tan^{-1}\frac{t}{3}\).
Restoring \(t=e^x\):
\(\therefore I=\frac{1}{2}\log(e^x+1)-\frac{1}{4}\log(e^{2x}+9)+\frac{1}{6}\tan^{-1}\frac{e^x}{3}+c\).

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key carries a spurious square root on the \(\log((\log x)^2+1)\) term (making its coefficient \(-\frac{5}{52}\) instead of \(-\frac{5}{26}\)) and gives the \(\tan^{-1}\) coefficient as \(\frac{11}{26}\) instead of \(\frac{12}{13}\). The answer below is correct.]

Put \(t=\log x\), so \(dt=\frac{dx}{x}\).
\(\therefore I=\int\frac{2t+3}{(3t+2)(t^2+1)}\,dt\).
Let \(\frac{2t+3}{(3t+2)(t^2+1)}=\frac{A}{3t+2}+\frac{Bt+C}{t^2+1}\Rightarrow 2t+3=A(t^2+1)+(Bt+C)(3t+2)\).
Put \(t=-\frac{2}{3}:\ \frac{5}{3}=A\left(\frac{13}{9}\right)\Rightarrow A=\frac{15}{13}\).
Compare \(t^2:\ 0=A+3B\Rightarrow B=-\frac{5}{13}\); constant: \(3=A+2C\Rightarrow C=\frac{12}{13}\).
\(\therefore I=\frac{15}{13}\int\frac{dt}{3t+2}+\frac{1}{13}\int\frac{-5t+12}{t^2+1}\,dt\).
\(=\frac{15}{13}\cdot\frac{1}{3}\log|3t+2|-\frac{5}{13}\cdot\frac{1}{2}\log(t^2+1)+\frac{12}{13}\tan^{-1}t\).
Restoring \(t=\log x\):
\(\therefore I=\frac{5}{13}\log|3\log x+2|-\frac{5}{26}\log\big((\log x)^2+1\big)+\frac{12}{13}\tan^{-1}(\log x)+c\).
